failure_analysis.what: Extracting the byte-by-byte state machine into a synchronous scanChunk function with ScanState marshaling caused a ~10% throughput regression (0.897 vs 0.946 baseline) instead of the expected 5-15% improvement.
failure_analysis.why: The per-chunk state object property reads/writes (11 fields marshaled in and out of scanChunk) introduced overhead that outweighed any gains from sync iteration. The benchmark input is an array of buffers, so the sync dispatch path was exercised, but the state marshaling cost dominated. The original inline for-await loop kept all state in local variables across chunks within the async function's frame, avoiding repeated property access.
failure_analysis.lesson: Extracting hot loops into separate functions requires careful attention to state marshaling cost. When the loop iterates millions of times (byte-by-byte) but state is only updated per-chunk, keeping the loop inline with persistent locals can be faster than function extraction with object-based state passing, even when the extracted function is synchronous. The plan's hypothesis that 'V8 optimizes plain functions better than async contexts' was correct in isolation, but the added state marshaling cost reversed the gain.
